description: A trail of links that shows where the current page sits in the site hierarchy.
overview:
A `Breadcrumb` is a labelled `nav` that contains a `BreadcrumbList`. The list holds `BreadcrumbItem` parts separated by `BreadcrumbSeparator` parts. Each item contains either a `BreadcrumbLink` to an ancestor page or, for the last item, a `BreadcrumbPage` for the current page. Use `BreadcrumbEllipsis` inside an item to stand in for collapsed levels.

Use breadcrumbs in deep hierarchies so people can see their location and move up quickly. For top-level navigation between sections, use a navigation menu or tabs.
usage:
Place a `BreadcrumbSeparator` between items as its own sibling, not inside a `BreadcrumbItem`. It renders a caret by default; pass children to use a different separator.

`BreadcrumbLink` renders an `a` by default. Use the `render` prop to render your router's link component instead.

For an icon-only link, such as a home icon, add an `aria-label`.

examples.WithHomeIcon: Replaces the first link with a home icon and an `aria-label`.
examples.CustomSeparator: Uses a slash instead of the default caret separator.

parts.Breadcrumb: The `nav` landmark that wraps the trail.
parts.BreadcrumbItem: A single step in the trail.
parts.BreadcrumbLink: A link to an ancestor page.
parts.BreadcrumbPage: The current page, rendered as plain text.
parts.BreadcrumbEllipsis: A placeholder for collapsed levels, with a screen-reader label.

accessibility:
- `Breadcrumb` renders a `nav` with `aria-label="breadcrumb"`.
- `BreadcrumbPage` sets `aria-current="page"`.
- Separators have `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden="true"`, so only items are announced as list items.
- `BreadcrumbEllipsis` hides its icon and includes visually hidden text, `More` by default; pass children to change it.
- Only links are in the tab order; the ellipsis and current page are skipped.
notes:
- Styling hooks: `data-slot` values from `breadcrumb` through `breadcrumb-ellipsis`.
- The default caret separator flips in right-to-left layouts.
- Ancestor links use `text-label-secondary` and the current page uses `text-label`.
